p3.text: Last Saturday, Jack went to the town with his aunt. First they went to the __(0)__ to buy some fruit. There were hundreds of people! Jack looked at a man with a big parrot, and when he looked again, his aunt wasn't there. Jack was __(1)__. He walked to the __(2)__ in the centre of the town, where there was a big clock. A kind __(3)__ asked him, 'Are you all right?' 'I can't find my aunt,' said Jack. The woman looked at the __(4)__ on her phone and phoned the market. Soon after, Jack's aunt came. She was very happy because she __(5)__ him. 'Now, hold my hand!' she said.

p4.title: Buses
p4.text: Buses are big cars __(0)__ can carry lots of people. In many towns, buses are red, green or yellow. People wait for the bus __(1)__ a bus stop. When the bus comes, they get on and show the driver __(2)__ buy a ticket. Some buses have two floors. Children love __(3)__ upstairs because they can see everything from the top. Buses are __(4)__ than cars, so more people can travel in one bus and the streets are not so busy. In some cities there __(5)__ buses at night, too.

parts.text: It was Saturday, and it was Grandpa's birthday. Lucy wanted to buy him a present, but she couldn't buy a big one. 'Let's go to the town,' said her mum. 'We can look in the shops.' They went by bus and got off in the town square.

examples.s: Lucy had only ___ to buy a present.

items.s: Lucy and her mum went to the town by ___.
They got off in the town ___.

parts.text: First they went to the clothes shop, but she couldn't buy a scarf there. Then they looked in the bookshop. Lucy saw a small book about birds. Grandpa loved birds! But the book was too big. Lucy was sad.

items.s: In the clothes shop, Lucy couldn't buy a ___.

parts.text: Then Lucy had an idea. In the market, she bought some paper and paints. At home, she painted a picture of Grandpa's favourite bird, a blue and yellow parrot. Grandpa loved it. 'This is the best present in the world,' he said, and he put it on the wall.

items.s: Lucy bought paper and paints in the ___.

p1.scene: Two pictures of the same street with a café. Left: the examiner's picture. Right: your picture.
p1.examiner: Look at the two pictures. Here the bus is red, but here the bus is green. What more differences can you see?
differences: In your picture there are two people at the bus stop, but in my picture there is one.
In your picture the dog is sitting, but in my picture it is running.
In your picture the café door is open, but in my picture it is closed.
In your picture the girl has got a scarf, but in my picture she has got a bag.
In your picture there are flowers in the window, but in my picture there aren't any.

p2.title: Fred and the lost dog
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'Fred and the lost dog'. Look at the pictures first. Fred is walking in the town with his mum. He sees a small dog next to a shop. It hasn't got a name on it and it looks sad. Now you tell the story.
frames: Fred is walking in the town with his mum. He sees a small sad dog next to a shop.
Fred and his mum take the dog to a shop near the park. A kind woman looks at the dog and phones someone.
A girl and her dad come to the shop. The girl is crying, but when she sees the dog she is very happy.
The girl takes the dog and says 'Thank you!' to Fred. Fred and the girl are now friends.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Look at this picture of our town, Kim. It's very busy today!
Who's the girl at the market, Dad? She's buying some fruit.
That's Sally. She lives next to us.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
Who's the man with the big box? He's coming out of the bookshop.
That's Fred. He works there. The box has got lots of new books in it.
Can you see the woman at the bus stop? She's got a baby.
Yes, that's Lily and her little boy. They're waiting for the bus to the hospital.
Look at that boy! He's on a skateboard.
That's Jack. He's very good, but he must be careful in the street.
And who's the girl with the map? She's got a camera too.
That's Zoe. She's from another town, so she doesn't know our streets.
She's taking a photo of the old clock.
Can you see the boy outside the café? He's eating an ice cream.
Yes, that's Tom. He always has a chocolate ice cream on Saturdays.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
There's a new library in the town, children.
It's in Park Street, opposite the café.
Park Street. Great, that's near my house.
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
What time does the library open?
It opens at nine o'clock in the morning.
Nine o'clock. And when does it close?
Is there a room for children?
Yes. It's called the Rainbow Room. R-A-I-N-B-O-W.
The Rainbow Room. Is it big?
Yes, and it's got lots of comics.
Can we go on the computers there?
Yes. There are twelve computers for children.
Yes, but only for a short time.
Yes. Story time is on Fridays at four o'clock.
Friday. I can go after school.
What do we need to bring?
Your library ticket. You need it to take books home.
My ticket. OK, I've got one.
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Mrs Long is telling Peter what she bought in each shop in the town. What did she buy in each place?
Hello, Mrs Long. You've got lots of bags!
Yes, Peter. I went to the market first. I bought some grapes. They're very sweet.
Can you see the letter G? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
Did you go to the bookshop?
Yes, I bought a comic for my grandson. It's about a shark. He loves sharks.
Then I went to the clothes shop. It's cold now, so I bought a scarf. A long red one.
Did you have a drink at the café?
Yes, and I bought a cake to take home. A chocolate cake for tea.
After that, I went to the toy shop. I bought a kite for my granddaughter. It's blue and green.
She can fly it in the park.
That's from the supermarket. Just some bread for dinner. Now I'm going home. Bye, Peter!
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
How is Jane going to the town centre?
Jane, are you going to the town centre by bus?
No, Dad. Mum is taking me in the car. My bike is broken.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
Excuse me, where's the bookshop? Is it next to the café?
No, it moved last year. Now it's opposite the school.
Two. What does Nick want to buy?
Nick, do you want a kite for your birthday?
No, Mum. I've got a ball and a kite. I want a robot! The one that walks.
A robot? Let's see how much it is.
Three. What is Dad doing now?
No, he's at the supermarket. He's doing the shopping.
No, he walked. It's very near.
Four. When does the shop close?
Excuse me, does the shop close at five o'clock?
No, we close at six. And on Saturdays we close at seven.
Six o'clock. OK, I can come back after school.
Five. What did Grandma lose in the town?
Grandma, did you lose your hat in the town?
No, my hat's here. I lost my glasses! I can't read the newspaper.
Did you leave them in your bag?
No, I looked in my bag. They're not there.
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Here's a picture of a street with some shops. Can you see the bus at the bus stop?
Yes, please. Colour the bus red.
Can you see the red bus? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the flowers in the window box?
There's a dog outside the café. Can I colour it?
Can you see the board above the shop door? It's empty.
Yes. Shall I write something on it?
Yes. Write the word 'toys'. T-O-Y-S. It's a toy shop.
Toys. OK, I'm writing it now.
Can I colour the car in the road?
Yes. What colour would you like?
And now the bird on the roof. Colour it yellow, please.
The bird on the roof. Yellow. Finished!
Well done. That's a lovely picture.
Now listen to Part Five again.
